raw.title: The Inward Umbrella
raw.normalExpectation: Pressing the button opens the canopy above, creating a dry shield.
raw.impossibleRule: The umbrella opens downward, wrapping around the user's body instead of above it, and always migrates to cover the lowest point.
raw.visibleTrigger: Opa presses the open button under rain; the canopy blooms down over his arm and torso, leaving his head wet.
raw.whyThisObject: An umbrella's entire purpose is to open into a dome over your head; inverting that dome makes it wrap you in wet fabric while rain still hits your exposed head.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action meant to create dry overhead space instead traps the body and concentrates rain onto the uncovered head, directly preventing dryness.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Opa stands in rain with a closed umbrella raised; the button has been pressed but the canopy has opened downward around his arm and upper body, his head exposed to downpour.

beats.strategy: Opa pulls the inverted canopy off his head and points the handle skyward, pressing button again to close.
beats.visibleConsequence: The wet fabric slides up his arm and seals around his neck like a collar, while rain soaks his exposed face.
beats.newInformation: The umbrella can't be removed by pulling; it migrates to the highest point of his body.

beats.strategy: Opa crouches low to the ground, hoping the umbrella will slide up to his raised hand.
beats.visibleConsequence: The canopy promptly engulfs his crouched back and legs, leaving only his feet sticking out, while rain pools on the fabric.
beats.newInformation: The umbrella always moves to cover the lowest body part, not the highest.

beats.strategy: Opa lies flat on the ground, spreading arms and legs to prevent any body part from being lowest.
beats.visibleConsequence: The umbrella flattens over his entire body like a tarp, but water runs off the edges and forms a puddle around him, soaking him from below.
beats.newInformation: Being covered doesn't stop water; it collects and soaks from ground contact.

beats.strategy: Opa rolls sideways toward a bus shelter, hoping to escape the rain while still covered.
beats.visibleConsequence: The umbrella rolls with him, wrapping around his torso like a soggy cocoon, and his head remains in the rain as he bumps into the shelter wall.
beats.newInformation: The umbrella's coverage deflects all rain away from any part it touches, concentrating rain onto uncovered head.

beats.strategy: Opa sits up inside the shelter, folds the umbrella manually by hand, and uses it as a normal hat.
beats.visibleConsequence: The umbrella stays open upside-down over his head, collecting rainwater that pours down his face inside the shelter.
beats.newInformation: The impossible orientation persists even when manually adjusted; any use creates a personal rain cloud.

raw.finalPayoff: The umbrella stays open upside-down over his head, collecting rainwater that pours down his face inside the shelter.
raw.loopPotential: Each new body position causes the umbrella to relocate to the lowest point, so Opa keeps trying to out-think the wrap but only changes which part gets covered.
raw.providerRationale: The protective function is reversed into a wet trap; visually clear because a downward-opening umbrella is instantly wrong for staying dry.

beats.quote: Opa stands in rain with a closed umbrella raised; the button has been pressed but the canopy has opened downward around his arm and upper body, his head exposed to downpour. Opa Opa pulls the inverted canopy off his head and points the handle skyward, pressing button again to close.. The wet fabric slides up his arm and seals around his neck like a collar, while rain soaks his exposed face. The umbrella can't be removed by pulling; it migrates to the highest point of his body.
beats.visual: Opa stands in rain with a closed umbrella raised; the button has been pressed but the canopy has opened downward around his arm and upper body, his head exposed to downpour. Opa Opa pulls the inverted canopy off his head and points the handle skyward, pressing button again to close.. The wet fabric slides up his arm and seals around his neck like a collar, while rain soaks his exposed face. The umbrella can't be removed by pulling; it migrates to the highest point of his body.

beats.quote: Opa Opa crouches low to the ground, hoping the umbrella will slide up to his raised hand.. The canopy promptly engulfs his crouched back and legs, leaving only his feet sticking out, while rain pools on the fabric. The umbrella always moves to cover the lowest body part, not the highest.
beats.visual: Opa Opa crouches low to the ground, hoping the umbrella will slide up to his raised hand.. The canopy promptly engulfs his crouched back and legs, leaving only his feet sticking out, while rain pools on the fabric. The umbrella always moves to cover the lowest body part, not the highest.

beats.quote: Opa Opa lies flat on the ground, spreading arms and legs to prevent any body part from being lowest.. The umbrella flattens over his entire body like a tarp, but water runs off the edges and forms a puddle around him, soaking him from below. Being covered doesn't stop water; it collects and soaks from ground contact.
beats.visual: Opa Opa lies flat on the ground, spreading arms and legs to prevent any body part from being lowest.. The umbrella flattens over his entire body like a tarp, but water runs off the edges and forms a puddle around him, soaking him from below. Being covered doesn't stop water; it collects and soaks from ground contact.

beats.quote: Opa Opa rolls sideways toward a bus shelter, hoping to escape the rain while still covered.. The umbrella rolls with him, wrapping around his torso like a soggy cocoon, and his head remains in the rain as he bumps into the shelter wall. The umbrella's coverage deflects all rain away from any part it touches, concentrating rain onto uncovered head.
beats.visual: Opa Opa rolls sideways toward a bus shelter, hoping to escape the rain while still covered.. The umbrella's coverage deflects all rain away from any part it touches, concentrating rain onto uncovered head.

The impossible orientation persists even when manually adjusted; any use creates a personal rain cloud.

raw.title: Self-Squeezing Toothpaste
raw.normalExpectation: Squeezing tube dispenses paste onto brush.
raw.impossibleRule: The tube squeezes itself from the bottom when cap is off, but any paste exiting immediately crawls back inside the nozzle when you squeeze manually.
raw.visibleTrigger: Kiko removes cap and paste oozes out on its own; when Kiko squeezes, the paste retracts.
raw.whyThisObject: Toothpaste is meant to be pushed out by external pressure; reversing cause and effect makes the tube act like a living creature controlling its contents.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: Every attempt to get paste onto brush results in either uncontrollable overflow or instant reattachment to tube, so brushing never gets paste.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Kiko holds a toothbrush ready while a toothpaste tube on the counter is already oozing a snake of paste upward; Kiko's other hand reaches to squeeze, but the paste begins sliding back into the nozzle.

beats.strategy: Kiko grabs the tube and squeezes hard to force paste onto brush.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ribbon of paste outside retracts fully into the nozzle, leaving brush dry.
beats.newInformation: Manual squeezing causes paste to be sucked back, opposite of normal.

beats.strategy: Kiko holds the tube upright and waits for it to ooze on its own, then brings brush underneath.
beats.visibleConsequence: Paste drips onto the brush but continues flowing, wrapping around bristles and gluing them into a blob.
beats.newInformation: The tube's self-squeeze never stops, creating an endless stream.

beats.strategy: Kiko yanks the brush away to break the paste stream.
beats.visibleConsequence: The paste string stretches and snaps, flinging the blob back onto Kiko's nose; the tube continues to ooze a new strand.
beats.newInformation: Breaking the stream causes projectile paste, and the tube refills itself instantly.

beats.strategy: Kiko caps the tube and uses a finger to scrape paste from his nose onto the brush.
beats.visibleConsequence: The tube starts shaking and expands, popping the cap off and spraying paste across the mirror.
beats.newInformation: The tube cannot be stopped by capping; pressure builds and releases violently.

beats.strategy: Kiko hides the tube in a drawer and quickly rubs the brush with the paste already on it.
beats.visibleConsequence: The drawer rattles, the tube rockets out, and a fresh paste snake lands directly on Kiko's tongue.
beats.newInformation: The tube actively targets Kiko's mouth, ensuring the paste reaches the goal but not via the brush.

raw.finalPayoff: The drawer rattles, the tube rockets out, and a fresh paste snake lands directly on Kiko's tongue.
raw.suggestedPayoffFamily: absurd success via object's own action
raw.loopPotential: Kiko might try closing the drawer, using a different tube, or catching the paste, but the tube always ejects paste onto his tongue exactly when he gives up.
raw.providerRationale: Toothpaste self-dispensing and refilling is a direct function inversion; the tube controls the paste rather than the user.

raw.title: Spiraling Shopping Cart
raw.everydayGoal: Push cart through supermarket to checkout
raw.normalExpectation: All four wheels swivel and roll straight when pushed.
raw.impossibleRule: Each wheel locks in alternating directions every time the cart moves, causing cart to travel in tightening spirals toward the store entrance.
raw.visibleTrigger: Mimi pushes forward, cart veers left and circles back.
raw.whyThisObject: Cart wheels are meant to provide straight mobility; locking their directions converts steering into a chaotic orbit.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The push intended to move cart forward instead causes a spiral away from checkout, preventing reaching the goal.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Mimi stands behind a shopping cart in an aisle, hands on handle, but all four wheels are pointed in different fixed angles; the cart has already begun a curved path back toward the entrance doors.

beats.strategy: Mimi pushes harder and straightens handle to go down aisle.
beats.visibleConsequence: The cart jerks right, then left, tracing a spiral that wraps around a cereal display.
beats.newInformation: Force increases turning radius instability, not direction control.

beats.strategy: Mimi tries to pull the cart backward, hoping the wheels unlock.
beats.visibleConsequence: The cart spins in place like a top, cans rattling, then accelerates forward in a new spiral toward the produce section.
beats.newInformation: Backward motion resets wheel angles to new random locks, worsening path.

beats.strategy: Mimi leans over and tries to rotate one wheel by hand while holding cart steady.
beats.visibleConsequence: The other three wheels snap to new positions, causing the cart to lurch sideways and knock over a stack of oranges.
beats.newInformation: Wheel directions are interdependent; adjusting one changes all.

beats.strategy: Mimi abandons pushing and drags the cart along the floor by its front corner.
beats.visibleConsequence: The cart tilts and rolls on two wheels, then slams down and spirals toward the automatic entrance, triggering doors to open.
beats.newInformation: The cart is stable only when moving sideways, but that still leads to exit.

beats.strategy: Mimi lets go of the cart and runs toward checkout, hoping to grab items and leave.
beats.visibleConsequence: The cart, still spiraling, bumps into Mimi from behind, pushing her through the checkout line and out the exit.
beats.newInformation: The cart's uncontrollable motion actively pursues Mimi, forcing her out of the store without paying.

raw.finalPayoff: The cart, still spiraling, bumps into Mimi from behind, pushing her through the checkout line and out the exit.
raw.loopPotential: Any attempt to steer or adjust wheels only creates a new spiral, and the cart inevitably herds Mimi toward the exit.
raw.environment: Supermarket aisle with checkout and automatic doors
raw.providerRationale: Wheels are for straight motion; reversing that into locked spirals is instantly intuitive and blocks shopping goal.

beats.strategy: Arda gives up and simply walks away, leaving the broom on the floor.

As he tilts pan, the pile dissolves and dirt races back to the original spot, leaving pan empty.
The delay is exactly two seconds, and any pause lets dirt escape.
Arda sweeps while holding dustpan in the other hand, moving both together.
Dirt enters the pan but then flies out backward through the bristles, returning to start.
The broom's bristles repel dirt when the pan is close, so dirt cannot be trapped.
Arda turns the broom over and uses the handle to push dirt like a rake.
The dirt stays put for a full three seconds, then jumps back even faster, scattering across a wider area.
Using a non-bristle part changes the delay to three seconds but increases speed of return.

raw.title: Vacuum Blows
raw.normalExpectation: Vacuum sucks air and debris into bag.
raw.impossibleRule: The vacuum blows air outward instead of sucking, scattering dust and crumbs toward the user's face and across the room.
raw.visibleTrigger: Luca turns it on, crumbs fly up and coat his glasses.
raw.whyThisObject: Vacuum's core function is negative pressure; reversing polarity turns cleaning into a debris storm.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action meant to remove crumbs instead propels them everywhere, making the room dirtier and preventing cleaning.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Luca pushes a vacuum over a carpet, but a cloud of dust and crumbs is erupting from the nozzle, covering his shoes and floating upward.

beats.strategy: Luca checks the bag and points nozzle away, turning it on again.
beats.visibleConsequence: A blast of air shoots out, knocking over a plant and spraying soil across the floor.
beats.newInformation: The motor polarity is reversed, so it's now a leaf blower.

beats.strategy: Luca reverses the vacuum's hose, attaching the other end to the front.
beats.visibleConsequence: The machine still blows, but now it sends air into its own bag, inflating it like a balloon until it pops.
beats.newInformation: Reversing the hose doesn't change airflow; it just pressurizes the containment.

beats.strategy: Luca holds the vacuum bag shut with his hand and tilts the nozzle toward a window.
beats.visibleConsequence: The bag inflates, lifts the vacuum off the floor, and starts flying around the room, spraying dust in circles.
beats.newInformation: The trapped air turns the vacuum into a thruster, causing uncontrolled flight.

beats.strategy: Luca unplugs the vacuum to stop the chaos.
beats.visibleConsequence: The vacuum falls to the floor and lets out a final puff of dust that settles exactly back onto the carpet.
beats.newInformation: Without power, the debris returns to its original position due to the reversed air pressure.

beats.strategy: Luca plugs it back in, but this time turns the power dial to 'max' hoping it will suck.
beats.visibleConsequence: The vacuum rockets forward, dragging Luca across the carpet and out the door, leaving a trail of sucked-up crumbs behind.
beats.newInformation: Max power reverses thrust direction, so the vacuum now sucks only when moving backward, dragging the user.

raw.finalPayoff: The vacuum rockets forward, dragging Luca across the carpet and out the door, leaving a trail of sucked-up crumbs behind.
raw.loopPotential: Each correction flips the airflow direction, but always in the opposite of what Luca expects, so he is alternately blown or dragged.
raw.providerRationale: Vacuum's suction reversed is instantly wrong; causing it to become a thruster adds absurd consequence.

raw.title: Mirrored Doorway
raw.normalExpectation: Opening a door leads to the room on the other side.
raw.impossibleRule: Whichever side of the door Noah opens, he steps into the same hallway but mirrored left-right.
raw.visibleTrigger: Noah opens kitchen door and sees hallway behind him without turning around.
raw.whyThisObject: A door is a threshold; if it teleports you back but mirrored, the transition is impossible to complete.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The act of crossing to the kitchen instead returns him to the hallway, preventing the goal.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Noah holds a door open; through the doorway is a reversed hallway identical to the one behind him, while a kitchen is visible in the mirror behind him.

beats.strategy: Noah steps through the doorway quickly, expecting to enter kitchen.
beats.visibleConsequence: He lands in a mirrored hallway, with door now behind him showing the kitchen as a reflection.
beats.newInformation: Passing through flips his orientation and swaps which side is real.

beats.strategy: Noah backs through the doorway, hoping to reverse the mirror effect.
beats.visibleConsequence: He ends up in the original hallway but now the door is on his left instead of right, and the kitchen is behind him.
beats.newInformation: Backing through does not cancel the flip; it just reorients his body.

beats.strategy: Noah tries to open the door from the mirrored hallway's other side.
beats.visibleConsequence: The door opens to an identical mirrored hallway nested inside, and Noah sees multiple copies of himself standing in doorways.
beats.newInformation: Each crossing creates a new mirrored copy of the same hallway, like an infinite recursion.

beats.strategy: Noah holds the door open with one hand and reaches through to touch the kitchen counter he can see in the reflection.
beats.visibleConsequence: His arm disappears through the doorway and emerges from a door behind him, tapping his own shoulder.
beats.newInformation: Space is folded so any object poked through wraps around to the starting side.

beats.strategy: Noah closes the door entirely, then opens it again while looking at his feet.
beats.visibleConsequence: He steps through and finds himself in the kitchen, but everything is mirrored—cabinets open the wrong way, and the clock runs backward.
beats.newInformation: The door finally allows entry, but the entire kitchen's handedness is reversed, so using it remains confusing.

raw.finalPayoff: He steps through and finds himself in the kitchen, but everything is mirrored—cabinets open the wrong way, and the clock runs backward.
raw.suggestedPayoffFamily: spatial rule change / goal reached with side effect
raw.loopPotential: Every additional door in the kitchen may also be mirrored, leading Noah to question every threshold.
raw.providerRationale: Door as threshold is subverted by self-mirroring; intuitive because you see same hallway where kitchen should be.

raw.title: Backward Alarm Clock
raw.everydayGoal: Wake up at 7 AM after setting alarm
raw.normalExpectation: Alarm rings at set time; hands move forward.
raw.impossibleRule: The clock's hands move backward whenever the alarm is set, so time appears to run in reverse; the alarm rings only when the hands return to midnight.
raw.visibleTrigger: Opa sets alarm for 7:00, the hour hand starts cranking counterclockwise.
raw.whyThisObject: Clock is meant to measure forward time; reversing hands makes scheduled wake-up impossible.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: Setting the alarm to a future time causes the clock to move backward away from that time, so the alarm will never ring at 7 AM.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Opa sits up in bed, staring at a bedside clock whose hour hand is moving backward past 6, while the alarm hand points to 7.

beats.strategy: Opa manually winds the clock forward to 6:59, expecting the alarm soon.
beats.visibleConsequence: As soon as he releases, the hands spin backward rapidly to 3:00.
beats.newInformation: Manual forward adjustment is undone by the reverse mechanism.

beats.strategy: Opa turns the alarm off and just watches the clock to see what time it shows.
beats.visibleConsequence: The hands freeze, then twitch backward one minute for every real second that passes.
beats.newInformation: Without alarm set, the clock still runs backward but slower.

beats.strategy: Opa sets the alarm for a time that already appears behind the current hand position, like 2:00, hoping it will trigger quickly.
beats.visibleConsequence: The alarm rings immediately, but the hands jump forward to noon, and the ringing reverses itself into a silent vacuum of sound.
beats.newInformation: Triggering the alarm causes time to jump forward to noon and sound to invert.

beats.strategy: Opa unplugs the clock and uses his phone to check the actual time.
beats.visibleConsequence: The clock's display reappears on his phone screen, showing the same backward time, and the phone's alarm icon turns into an hourglass.
beats.newInformation: The clock's impossible rule spreads to other time-keeping devices.

beats.strategy: Opa gives up and falls back asleep.
beats.visibleConsequence: The clock chimes twelve times in reverse, and Opa wakes up at 7 AM, but the clock reads 7 PM.
beats.newInformation: The backward time eventually catches up to the correct wake hour, but day and night are swapped.

raw.finalPayoff: The clock chimes twelve times in reverse, and Opa wakes up at 7 AM, but the clock reads 7 PM.
raw.suggestedPayoffFamily: delayed consequence / goal reached wrongly via causal inversion
raw.loopPotential: If Opa trusts the clock, he'll sleep through day; if he ignores it, he wakes on time but distrusts all clocks.
raw.providerRationale: Clock's directional time reversal directly prevents scheduled waking; the impossible rule is visually obvious with backward hands.

raw.title: Neighbor's TV Remote
raw.everydayGoal: Change channel to watch favorite show
raw.normalExpectation: Pressing buttons changes your own TV channel.
raw.impossibleRule: The remote's signal always targets the neighbor's television through the wall, changing their channel while your TV stays off.
raw.visibleTrigger: Kiko presses power; neighbor yells, but Kiko's TV remains black.
raw.whyThisObject: Remote is designed to control one specific TV; misdirecting signal to wrong TV makes it useless for your goal.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The intended action of controlling your TV instead controls someone else's, so your show cannot be selected.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Kiko points remote at his dark TV, but through the apartment wall, the neighbor's TV screen is visibly flickering channels, and the neighbor's shouting bubble appears.

beats.strategy: Kiko moves closer to his TV, pressing power repeatedly.
beats.visibleConsequence: The neighbor's TV volume increases to maximum, shaking the wall, while Kiko's screen stays off.
beats.newInformation: Distance doesn't matter; the remote's signal is hardwired to the neighbor's set.

beats.strategy: Kiko covers the remote's IR emitter with his hand, hoping to block scatter.
beats.visibleConsequence: The neighbor's TV turns off and on rapidly, causing a strobe effect through the window.
beats.newInformation: Blocking the emitter still sends an encoded signal that only the neighbor's TV understands.

beats.strategy: Kiko opens his TV's manual buttons and tries to change channel directly.
beats.visibleConsequence: The neighbor's TV switches to a karaoke channel, and the neighbor starts singing loudly, while Kiko's TV ignores the manual buttons.
beats.newInformation: Any input intended for Kiko's TV is transferred to the neighbor's TV due to a crossed signal wire.

beats.strategy: Kiko unplugs his TV to 'reset' the remote link.
beats.visibleConsequence: The neighbor's TV turns off and then on, now showing Kiko's living room via a hidden camera feed.
beats.newInformation: The link is now bidirectional; the neighbor's TV displays Kiko's actions.

beats.strategy: Kiko goes next door to ask the neighbor to change their channel to Kiko's show.
beats.visibleConsequence: The neighbor agrees, but when they press their own remote, Kiko's TV turns on and changes to a cooking show.
beats.newInformation: The cross-wiring is symmetrical: neighbor's remote controls Kiko's TV.

raw.finalPayoff: The neighbor agrees, but when they press their own remote, Kiko's TV turns on and changes to a cooking show.
raw.loopPotential: Kiko could swap remotes with neighbor, but that might swap their TVs entirely, leading to endless confusion.
raw.environment: Apartment living room with thin wall to neighbor
raw.providerRationale: Remote's targeted control is rerouted to wrong device; visually funny when neighbor reacts and your screen stays dark.

raw.title: Ceiling Pancake
raw.normalExpectation: A quick wrist flip sends pancake up and back into pan.
raw.impossibleRule: The pan exerts a vertical launch force so strong that any food flies upward and sticks to the ceiling; the pan then becomes too slippery to hold.
raw.visibleTrigger: Mimi flips the pancake; it rockets to ceiling and stays.
raw.whyThisObject: Pan's function is to toss food for cooking; if toss becomes permanent adhesion, cooking is impossible.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The flipping action meant to turn the pancake instead removes it from the pan and glues it overhead, preventing eating.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Mimi holds a frying pan, looking up; a pancake is stuck flat on the ceiling, and a second pancake arcs upward from the pan.

beats.strategy: Mimi scrapes the pancake off the ceiling with a spatula, then tries a gentler flip.
beats.visibleConsequence: The pancake still leaps up and splats on ceiling, sticking even harder.
beats.newInformation: The launch force is independent of wrist strength.

beats.strategy: Mimi holds a plate over the pan and flips, hoping to catch the pancake.
beats.visibleConsequence: The pancake punches through the plate, sending shards flying, and both pancake and plate fragments stick to ceiling.
beats.newInformation: The launched food has enough force to penetrate obstacles.

beats.strategy: Mimi turns off the stove and waits for the pancake to fall.
beats.visibleConsequence: The pancake slowly peels off the ceiling and falls back into the pan, but immediately turns black and smokes.
beats.newInformation: The pancake's fall is controlled by cooking timer, not gravity; it returns overcooked.

beats.strategy: Mimi tries to cook without flipping, using a lid to steam.
beats.visibleConsequence: The pan's handle starts vibrating, and all the batter in the pan spontaneously flips itself to the ceiling in one big sheet.
beats.newInformation: The pan's flipping rule applies to any batter inside, even without a wrist motion.

beats.strategy: Mimi gives up and turns off the stove, leaving the pan on the counter.
beats.visibleConsequence: The pan itself flips upward, sticks to the ceiling, and the pancake falls onto Mimi's head.
beats.newInformation: The pan's upward launch now applies to itself, completing the role reversal.

raw.finalPayoff: The pan itself flips upward, sticks to the ceiling, and the pancake falls onto Mimi's head.
raw.loopPotential: Any cooking utensil in this kitchen may also launch upward, forcing Mimi to cook with ceiling-mounted tools.
raw.providerRationale: Pan's flip function is exaggerated into ceiling adhesion; visually clear and blocks eating.

raw.title: Kettle Rain Cloud
raw.normalExpectation: Kettle boils water, steam escapes, hot water pours into cup.
raw.impossibleRule: Boiling water evaporates into a small rain cloud that follows the kettle, and the rain falls only when you try to pour, often into your face or elsewhere.
raw.visibleTrigger: Arda boils kettle, a mini cloud forms above it; when he tilts, rain falls on his hand.
raw.whyThisObject: Kettle's steam should dissipate; if it condenses into a mobile cloud, it steals the water before it can be poured.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The water never stays liquid to pour; it becomes a cloud that rains unpredictably, preventing tea.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Arda holds a boiling kettle with a tiny gray cloud hovering just above the spout; small raindrops fall onto his sleeve.

beats.strategy: Arda waves away the cloud and quickly pours into a cup.
beats.visibleConsequence: The cloud darts under the stream, catching all the water as it pours, leaving the cup dry.
beats.newInformation: The cloud can intercept the stream, so water becomes rain before reaching cup.

beats.strategy: Arda holds the cup over the kettle spout to catch water before cloud intercepts.
beats.visibleConsequence: The cloud squeezes through the spout and rains inside the cup, but the water immediately evaporates back up to the cloud.
beats.newInformation: Any liquid water in the cup is reabsorbed by the cloud due to its attachment to the kettle's heat.

beats.strategy: Arda puts the kettle in the refrigerator to cool the cloud down.
beats.visibleConsequence: The cloud starts snowing, covering Arda's hand and the counter with frost, while the kettle remains hot.
beats.newInformation: Cooling the environment changes the cloud's precipitation but not its stealing behavior.

beats.strategy: Arda tilts the kettle and holds an umbrella over his head.
beats.visibleConsequence: The cloud expands into a full room-wide rainstorm, soaking everything except the cup.
beats.newInformation: The cloud's size scales with attempts to shield from it.

beats.strategy: Arda unplugs the kettle and uses a microwave to heat water directly.
beats.visibleConsequence: The cloud follows the kettle, which now flies off the counter and hovers over the microwave, raining into it and shorting the appliance.
beats.newInformation: The cloud is bonded to the kettle object, not the heating method, and it actively prevents any other water heating.

raw.finalPayoff: The cloud follows the kettle, which now flies off the counter and hovers over the microwave, raining into it and shorting the appliance.
raw.loopPotential: Arda might use a different kettle, but the cloud may transfer to that one, chasing any boiling attempt.
raw.providerRationale: Kettle's steam condensing into a thieving rain cloud is intuitive and directly blocks tea.

raw.title: Dirtying Soap
raw.normalExpectation: Rubbing soap with water removes dirt.
raw.impossibleRule: Soap transfers dirt from the sink onto hands, making them grimier with every scrub; when rinsed, the soap laughs and re-dirties the water.
raw.visibleTrigger: Luca rubs soap, hands turn black.
raw.whyThisObject: Soap's chemical action is to lift dirt; reversing it makes soap a dirt magnet that deposits grime.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The act of washing applies more dirt, so hands never become clean.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Luca stands at sink with soapy hands, but his hands are covered in dark grime, and the soap bar is pristine white while black suds flow down the drain.

beats.strategy: Luca rinses hands thoroughly under water.
beats.visibleConsequence: The water runs black, but his hands remain black, and the soap bar floats over and touches his elbow, transferring more grime.
beats.newInformation: Rinsing does not remove soap's dirt; the soap actively reattaches to skin.

beats.strategy: Luca uses a nail brush to scrub the grime off.
beats.visibleConsequence: The brush strokes push the grime deeper into his skin, making his hands look like charcoal.
beats.newInformation: Any friction with the grime helps it penetrate, not remove.

beats.strategy: Luca switches to liquid soap from a bottle.
beats.visibleConsequence: The liquid soap pours out as black goo and coats the bar soap, which then leaps into Luca's pocket, staining his clothes.
beats.newInformation: All soaps in the environment are contaminated and transfer grime to any surface.

beats.strategy: Luca dries his hands with a paper towel.
beats.visibleConsequence: The towel tears away a layer of grime but reveals a second layer of different colored dirt underneath.
beats.newInformation: The dirt is layered, and removing the top layer just exposes the next.

beats.strategy: Luca gives up and leaves the bathroom, hands black.
beats.visibleConsequence: The soap bar follows him, bouncing along the floor, and wherever it touches, grime appears, making a trail.
beats.newInformation: The soap's dirt-creating ability extends beyond hands to the environment.

raw.finalPayoff: The soap bar follows him, bouncing along the floor, and wherever it touches, grime appears, making a trail.
raw.loopPotential: Luca can try other cleaning products, but they may all become dirt generators due to the soap's influence.
raw.providerRationale: Soap's cleaning action reversed into dirt application is a direct function inversion with messy visual payoff.

Any friction with the grime helps it penetrate, not remove.
Luca switches to liquid soap from a bottle.
The liquid soap pours out as black goo and coats the bar soap, which then leaps into Luca's pocket, staining his clothes.
All soaps in the environment are contaminated and transfer grime to any surface.

The dirt is layered, and removing the top layer just exposes the next.
Luca gives up and leaves the bathroom, hands black.
The soap bar follows him, bouncing along the floor, and wherever it touches, grime appears, making a trail.

raw.title: Self-Healing Paper
raw.normalExpectation: Scissors shear paper into two pieces.
raw.impossibleRule: As scissors cut, the paper immediately heals behind the blades, leaving no cut; the scissors themselves become slightly more blunt.
raw.visibleTrigger: Kiko snips a paper, the cut line closes seamlessly.
raw.whyThisObject: Scissors are meant to divide material; if the material self-heals, the cutting action is futile.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The intended cut never persists, so crafting cannot proceed.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Kiko holds scissors mid-snip on a paper; the cut line behind the blades is sealing itself closed, with no separation visible.

beats.strategy: Kiko cuts faster, moving scissors along a straight line.
beats.visibleConsequence: The paper zips back together instantly, and the scissors make a zipper-like sound.
beats.newInformation: Speed of cutting increases the healing speed equally.

beats.strategy: Kiko folds the paper and cuts through multiple layers.
beats.visibleConsequence: The layers fuse together at the cut line, creating a thicker uncut stack.
beats.newInformation: Cutting multiple layers causes them to weld, not separate.

beats.strategy: Kiko uses a craft knife instead of scissors.
beats.visibleConsequence: The knife blade passes through but the paper instantly reattaches, and the knife's edge dulls to a butter knife shape.
beats.newInformation: The self-healing effect applies to any cutting tool and dulls the blade.

beats.strategy: Kiko tries to tear the paper by hand.
beats.visibleConsequence: The paper stretches like rubber and bounces back, flipping out of his hands.
beats.newInformation: The paper has become elastic, so it cannot be cut or torn.

beats.strategy: Kiko gives up and tries to use pre-cut paper shapes from a packet.
beats.visibleConsequence: The pre-cut shapes snap back into full sheets, and the scissors in his hand leap to the paper and start 'cutting' but leaving no marks.
beats.newInformation: The rule reverses relationship: tools cuts but material refuses to remain divided; even pre-existing cuts are undone.

raw.finalPayoff: The pre-cut shapes snap back into full sheets, and the scissors in his hand leap to the paper and start 'cutting' but leaving no marks.
raw.loopPotential: Any future cutting attempt heals; Kiko might try water or fire, but risk of new escalation.
raw.providerRationale: Scissors' dividing function is negated by self-healing paper; intuitive because cut line zips shut.

raw.title: Bottom-Opening Zipper
raw.everydayGoal: Zip up jacket to stay warm
raw.normalExpectation: Pulling zipper up closes the jacket.
raw.impossibleRule: As you pull the zipper tab upward, the bottom of the zipper separates, so the jacket opens from bottom while top closes; when you pull down, the bottom closes but top opens.
raw.visibleTrigger: Mimi zips up to neck; the jacket's bottom half splits open, exposing her stomach.
raw.whyThisObject: Zipper is designed to interlock teeth sequentially; if it opens opposite end, the closure is incomplete.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action to close the jacket creates an opening elsewhere, so warmth cannot be retained.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Mimi holds zipper tab at neck, jacket top is closed, but the bottom half hangs open, cold air whooshing through.

beats.strategy: Mimi pulls zipper down to close the bottom gap.
beats.visibleConsequence: The bottom zips shut but the top splits down to her chest.
beats.newInformation: The zipper has a pivot point; one end opens as the other closes.

beats.strategy: Mimi holds the bottom together with one hand while zipping up with the other.
beats.visibleConsequence: The zipper teeth at her hand pop apart, and her fingers get caught between them.
beats.newInformation: Physical holding doesn't prevent separation; the zipper actively parts around any obstruction.

beats.strategy: Mimi zips halfway, hoping the middle stays closed.
beats.visibleConsequence: Both top and bottom open outward like a mouth, and the jacket flaps open completely.
beats.newInformation: Halfway position opens both ends simultaneously.

beats.strategy: Mimi turns the jacket inside out and zips from the other side.
beats.visibleConsequence: The zipper now unzips from the middle, splitting the jacket into two separate halves that fall to the floor.
beats.newInformation: The zipper's failure mode changes with orientation, now bisects the garment.

beats.strategy: Mimi grabs a safety pin to pin the bottom closed.
beats.visibleConsequence: The safety pin zips itself into the zipper track and the entire jacket rolls up like a window blind, squeezing Mimi's torso.
beats.newInformation: The zipper treats any inserted object as a pull tab and activates full closure upward, trapping Mimi.

raw.finalPayoff: The safety pin zips itself into the zipper track and the entire jacket rolls up like a window blind, squeezing Mimi's torso.
raw.loopPotential: Further attempts to unfasten may cause the jacket to roll or unroll unpredictably.
raw.providerRationale: Zipper's interlocking action is spatially inverted, so closing one end opens the other; visually clear and blocks warmth.

originalInput.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: As you pull the zipper tab upward, the bottom of the zipper separates, so the jacket opens from bottom while top closes; when you pull down, the bottom closes but top opens.
originalInput.frameZeroDescription: Mimi holds zipper tab at neck, jacket top is closed, but the bottom half hangs open, cold air whooshing through. Mimi Mimi pulls zipper down to close the bottom gap.. The bottom zips shut but the top splits down to her chest. The zipper has a pivot point; one end opens as the other closes.

escalationPlan.description: Mimi holds zipper tab at neck, jacket top is closed, but the bottom half hangs open, cold air whooshing through. Mimi Mimi pulls zipper down to close the bottom gap.. The bottom zips shut but the top splits down to her chest. The zipper has a pivot point; one end opens as the other closes.

Mimi Mimi holds the bottom together with one hand while zipping up with the other.. The zipper teeth at her hand pop apart, and her fingers get caught between them. Physical holding doesn't prevent separation; the zipper actively parts around any obstruction.
Mimi Mimi zips halfway, hoping the middle stays closed.. Both top and bottom open outward like a mouth, and the jacket flaps open completely. Halfway position opens both ends simultaneously.

Mimi Mimi turns the jacket inside out and zips from the other side.. The zipper now unzips from the middle, splitting the jacket into two separate halves that fall to the floor. The zipper's failure mode changes with orientation, now bisects the garment.

Mimi Mimi grabs a safety pin to pin the bottom closed.. The safety pin zips itself into the zipper track and the entire jacket rolls up like a window blind, squeezing Mimi's torso. The zipper treats any inserted object as a pull tab and activates full closure upward, trapping Mimi.

originalInput.finalPayoff: Mimi Mimi grabs a safety pin to pin the bottom closed.. The safety pin zips itself into the zipper track and the entire jacket rolls up like a window blind, squeezing Mimi's torso. The zipper treats any inserted object as a pull tab and activates full closure upward, trapping Mimi.

raw.title: Bottomless Backpack
raw.normalExpectation: Items placed in top stay inside until you open it.
raw.impossibleRule: The bottom of the backpack opens whenever it is upright; when turned upside down, the bottom seals but the top opens, so contents always spill.
raw.visibleTrigger: Arda puts books in upright backpack; they fall through bottom onto floor.
raw.whyThisObject: Backpack is a container; if gravity works against the orientation, it cannot hold items.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The act of placing items inside directly causes them to exit through bottom, preventing packing.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Arda holds a backpack upright with several books halfway falling through the open bottom, while the top zipper is closed.

beats.strategy: Arda turns the backpack upside down to use the sealed bottom as top.
beats.visibleConsequence: The original top zipper opens, and books pour out onto his head.
beats.newInformation: The pack has two openings, and gravity always finds the open one.

beats.strategy: Arda holds the backpack sideways and loads books through the side.
beats.visibleConsequence: A new side seam splits open, and all contents slide out horizontally.
beats.newInformation: Any orientation creates a new opening at the lowest point.

beats.strategy: Arda stuffs clothes into the bottom to block it, then adds books.
beats.visibleConsequence: The clothes squeeze through the bottom seam, pulling the books with them, leaving an empty flattened pack.
beats.newInformation: The bottom opening acts like a drain that vacuums contents out.

beats.strategy: Arda puts the backpack on his back, hoping body pressure seals the bottom.
beats.visibleConsequence: The pack inflates and launches off his shoulders, spinning in midair as contents rainbow out.
beats.newInformation: Wearing the pack triggers ejection, not sealing.

beats.strategy: Arda gives up and carries books in his arms.
beats.visibleConsequence: The backpack slides over and swallows the books from his arms, then spits them out the bottom into a neat pile at his feet.
beats.newInformation: The pack wants to be filled but immediately empties itself as soon as it contains anything.

raw.finalPayoff: The backpack slides over and swallows the books from his arms, then spits them out the bottom into a neat pile at his feet.
raw.loopPotential: Any future loading attempt triggers the same drain; Arda might need a bottomless bag that is actually bottomless.

The pack has two openings, and gravity always finds the open one.

escalationPlan.description: Arda holds a backpack upright with several books halfway falling through the open bottom, while the top zipper is closed. Arda Arda turns the backpack upside down to use the sealed bottom as top.. The original top zipper opens, and books pour out onto his head. The pack has two openings, and gravity always finds the open one.

Arda Arda holds the backpack sideways and loads books through the side.. A new side seam splits open, and all contents slide out horizontally. Any orientation creates a new opening at the lowest point.

Arda Arda stuffs clothes into the bottom to block it, then adds books.. The clothes squeeze through the bottom seam, pulling the books with them, leaving an empty flattened pack. The bottom opening acts like a drain that vacuums contents out.

Arda Arda puts the backpack on his back, hoping body pressure seals the bottom.. The pack inflates and launches off his shoulders, spinning in midair as contents rainbow out. Wearing the pack triggers ejection, not sealing.

Arda Arda gives up and carries books in his arms.. The backpack slides over and swallows the books from his arms, then spits them out the bottom into a neat pile at his feet. The pack wants to be filled but immediately empties itself as soon as it contains anything.

originalInput.finalPayoff: Arda Arda gives up and carries books in his arms.. The backpack slides over and swallows the books from his arms, then spits them out the bottom into a neat pile at his feet. The pack wants to be filled but immediately empties itself as soon as it contains anything.

raw.title: Self-Tucking Bed Sheets
raw.everydayGoal: Get out of bed in the morning
raw.normalExpectation: You push sheets off and stand up.
raw.impossibleRule: The more you push sheets away, the tighter they tuck around your body; sheets re-tuck themselves under the mattress as you move.
raw.visibleTrigger: Luca throws off blanket; it snaps back over him.
raw.whyThisObject: Bedsheets are meant to cover; if they actively trap, getting up becomes a wrestling match.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action to remove sheets causes them to rewrap, preventing standing.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Luca lies in bed with one leg out, but the sheet has wrapped around his leg and is pulling him back toward the mattress.

beats.strategy: Luca sits up and pushes the sheet to the foot of the bed.
beats.visibleConsequence: The sheet springs back and tucks itself under his chin, pinning his arms to his sides.
beats.newInformation: The sheet's fabric is elastic and self-tucking.

beats.strategy: Luca rolls toward the edge to slide out.
beats.visibleConsequence: The sheet rolls with him, winding around his torso like a burrito.
beats.newInformation: Moving doesn't loosen; it increases winding.

beats.strategy: Luca kicks violently to break the wrap.
beats.visibleConsequence: The sheet stretches into ropes that tie his ankles to the bed frame.
beats.newInformation: The sheet can transform into adjustable restraints, comedic but not harmful.

beats.strategy: Luca tries to crawl out from the bottom of the bed.
beats.visibleConsequence: The fitted sheet pops off the mattress and becomes a parachute, dragging him back to the center.
beats.newInformation: The whole sheet detaches and acts as a net.

beats.strategy: Luca calls for help, and Mimi enters to pull him out.
beats.visibleConsequence: The sheet wraps around both of them, tucking them together like a mummy, while the bed bounces.
beats.newInformation: The sheet's tucking extends to anyone who tries to intervene.

raw.finalPayoff: The sheet wraps around both of them, tucking them together like a mummy, while the bed bounces.
raw.suggestedPayoffFamily: goal blocked by self-tucking / role reversal
raw.loopPotential: Any morning, Luca will be held by sheets until the bed decides to release him.
raw.providerRationale: Bedsheets' covering function becomes trapping; intuitive because throwing off sheets should free you, not rewrap you.

raw.title: Random Fridge Interior
raw.normalExpectation: Opening door reveals same contents each time.
raw.impossibleRule: Each time the fridge door opens, the interior is a different environment (a desert, a freezer landscape, a tropical beach, etc.), making food retrieval impossible.
raw.visibleTrigger: Noah opens door expecting milk, sees a small snowstorm inside.
raw.whyThisObject: Fridge is a stable storage box; if interior is random, it can't store food.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action of opening to get milk reveals random non-milk content, preventing goal.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Noah holds fridge door open, but inside is a miniature glacier with a penguin; no shelves or milk carton.

beats.strategy: Noah closes and reopens the fridge, hoping for the normal interior.
beats.visibleConsequence: Now the interior is a tropical rainforest with waterfalls; a pineapple rolls out.
beats.newInformation: Each opening cycles through random biome, never the kitchen fridge.

beats.strategy: Noah reaches in past the environment to feel for the milk carton.
beats.visibleConsequence: His hand comes back holding a coconut, and the rainforest interior shuts around his arm, trapping him briefly.
beats.newInformation: Objects inside are real and can interact, but not his groceries.

beats.strategy: Noah holds the door open and waits, watching the interior change.
beats.visibleConsequence: The environment morphs every three seconds, cycling through desert, ocean, wardrobe, and a copy of the kitchen seen from behind.
beats.newInformation: The fridge's interior is a portal to other places, not a storage space.

beats.strategy: Noah puts on a coat and steps into the fridge to search.
beats.visibleConsequence: The door closes and reopens, showing Noah inside a snowy tundra waving from behind a glass door in another country.
beats.newInformation: Entering the fridge transports the person to the biome, not to the groceries.

beats.strategy: Noah unplugs the fridge, expecting it to reset.
beats.visibleConsequence: The door pops open, and a blast of cold air covers the kitchen in frost; the milk carton appears on top of the fridge, frozen solid.
beats.newInformation: Turning off power deposits the missing milk outside the fridge, but frozen and unusable.

raw.suggestedPayoffFamily: environmental takeover / goal object appears unusable
raw.loopPotential: Noah might try a mini-fridge, but it could have similar portal properties.

raw.title: Microwave Hot Plate
raw.normalExpectation: Microwave heats food evenly.
raw.impossibleRule: The microwave heats the plate to scalding while food remains frozen solid; any attempt to remove plate transfers heat to food, flash-thawing it but also melting plate.
raw.visibleTrigger: Opa opens microwave, plate glows red, food has ice crystals.
raw.whyThisObject: Microwave's energy is meant to excite water in food; if it excites the plate material, food stays cold.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action of heating food results in dangerous hot plate and cold food, preventing eating.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Opa opens microwave, steam rises from the plate, but the food on it is visibly frozen with frost.

beats.strategy: Opa uses oven mitts to remove the hot plate.
beats.visibleConsequence: The mitts start smoking, and the plate's heat melts a hole through the mitt, dropping the plate onto the counter, which sizzles.
beats.newInformation: The plate is hotter than expected; it transfers heat outward.

beats.strategy: Opa runs the plate under cold water to cool it.
beats.visibleConsequence: The water flashes to steam, and the food thaws instantly but is now soggy and boiling.
beats.newInformation: Water contact transfers heat to food but also overcooks it.

beats.strategy: Opa puts the frozen food on a different plate and microwaves again.
beats.visibleConsequence: The new plate heats red, food remains frozen, and the microwave's glass window fogs.
beats.newInformation: The microwave always targets the plate material, not food.

beats.strategy: Opa tries to microwave the food without a plate, directly on the turntable.
beats.visibleConsequence: The microwave refuses to start, beeping and displaying 'PLATE REQUIRED' in glowing letters.
beats.newInformation: The appliance demands a plate to activate, ensuring impossible heating.

beats.strategy: Opa gives up and eats the frozen food directly.
beats.visibleConsequence: The hot plate jumps from counter onto Opa's lap, thawing the food on his fork instantly but also scorching his pants.
beats.newInformation: The plate can transfer its heat to the food when close, but always at the cost of burning surroundings.

raw.finalPayoff: The hot plate jumps from counter onto Opa's lap, thawing the food on his fork instantly but also scorching his pants.
raw.loopPotential: Any reheat attempt repeats the plate heating; Opa might use a metal plate, causing sparks (child-safe comedic but not shown?).
raw.providerRationale: Microwave's selective heating is subverted; visually clear with ice on food and glowing plate.

raw.title: Wrong-Room Light Switch
raw.normalExpectation: Flipping switch controls nearest room's light.
raw.impossibleRule: The switch controls the light in a different room (e.g., bathroom), while the room you're in stays dark; each switch in house controls a random other room.
raw.visibleTrigger: Kiko flips living room switch; hall light turns on, living room dark.
raw.whyThisObject: Light switches are spatially tied to their room; cross-wiring makes them useless for local control.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action to illuminate your room instead lights a distant room, leaving you in dark.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Kiko stands in dark living room flipping a switch; through the doorway, the bathroom light is on, and the living room remains dark.

beats.strategy: Kiko flips the switch repeatedly, hoping to get the right room.
beats.visibleConsequence: Various lights in the house turn on and off in a pattern, but the living room stays dark while the porch light blinks.
beats.newInformation: The switch cycles through all other rooms except the one he's in.

beats.strategy: Kiko walks to the bathroom to flip that switch.
beats.visibleConsequence: The bathroom light turns off, and the living room light turns on.
beats.newInformation: Switches are paired with opposite rooms; you must be in the room you don't want lit.

beats.strategy: Kiko stands in the doorway between rooms to flip both switches.
beats.visibleConsequence: Both rooms go dark, and a flickering light appears in the attic.
beats.newInformation: Simultaneous toggles transfer power to an unswitched room.

beats.strategy: Kiko uses a flashlight to see while navigating the switch panel.
beats.visibleConsequence: The flashlight turns on, but its beam illuminates the wrong room through a window, and Kiko stumbles.
beats.newInformation: The cross-wiring extends to all light sources, including portable ones.

beats.strategy: Kiko gives up and uses candles.
beats.visibleConsequence: The candles' flames cast shadows that point to a hidden switch behind a bookshelf; flipping that switch turns on the sun outside, causing full daylight indoors.
beats.newInformation: There is a master switch that controls daylight, not indoor lights, solving the darkness but at absurd scale.

raw.finalPayoff: The candles' flames cast shadows that point to a hidden switch behind a bookshelf; flipping that switch turns on the sun outside, causing full daylight indoors.
raw.suggestedPayoffFamily: unexpected causal success via wrong switch
raw.loopPotential: The daylight switch may reset at night, forcing Kiko to find another hidden control.
raw.providerRationale: Light switch's local function is scrambled; intuitive because you see wrong room light up.

raw.normalExpectation: Water flows downward out of spout into glass.

raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action to fill glass causes water to go the wrong way, so glass never fills.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Mimi holds a glass under a faucet, but a vertical stream of water shoots upward to the ceiling, and none falls into the glass.

beats.strategy: Mimi holds the glass above the faucet, upside down, to catch the upward stream.
beats.visibleConsequence: The water flows into the glass but immediately shoots out the top like a second fountain, emptying it.
beats.newInformation: The water's upward momentum continues through any container.

beats.strategy: Mimi turns the faucet off and collects the falling rainwater that comes down.
beats.visibleConsequence: The rain falls directly around the sink but not into the glass, and the glass itself floats upward.
beats.newInformation: When faucet is off, water falls, but the glass becomes buoyant and rises away.

beats.strategy: Mimi puts a lid on the glass and stands on a chair to catch water at ceiling level.

beats.newInformation: The ceiling acts as a reservoir; water gathers there and traps containers.

beats.strategy: Mimi uses a bucket and mop to sweep water from ceiling down.
beats.visibleConsequence: The bucket also floats up and sticks to ceiling, splashing water everywhere but down.
beats.newInformation: Objects near the upward flow become anti-gravity and collect on ceiling.

beats.visibleConsequence: The water stops, and all the ceiling water falls at once, filling the room waist-deep and floating the glass to Mimi.
beats.newInformation: Shutting off the valve releases the accumulated water all at once, causing a flood but delivering the glass.

raw.title: Collapsing Chair
raw.normalExpectation: Chair supports weight when sat on.
raw.impossibleRule: The chair remains rigid when empty, but the instant any weight is applied, its legs fold flat, dropping occupant to floor; when empty, it pops back upright.
raw.visibleTrigger: Arda sits, chair flattens beneath him.
raw.whyThisObject: Chair's structural function is support; conditional collapse makes sitting impossible.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action of sitting triggers the loss of support, so you can never rest in chair.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Arda is mid-air just above a chair that has collapsed flat on the floor, legs splayed outward.

beats.strategy: Arda checks the chair, stands it up, and presses on the seat with one hand.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair collapses instantly under the light hand pressure, then springs back.
beats.newInformation: Even partial weight triggers collapse; no weight means rigid.

beats.strategy: Arda tries to sit very slowly, easing weight onto the seat.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair collapses progressively, lowering him to the floor in a controlled slide, then snaps shut on his fingers.
beats.newInformation: Slow approach doesn't prevent collapse; it just prolongs the drop.

beats.strategy: Arda puts a stack of books on the chair to hold it steady.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair stays upright, but when Arda sits on the books, the chair collapses sideways and books scatter.
beats.newInformation: Distributed weight still triggers collapse as long as it includes Arda.

beats.strategy: Arda stands on the chair instead of sitting.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair flings him forward like a catapult, launching him onto the desk.
beats.newInformation: The chair's collapse mechanism can store and release energy when weight is applied.

beats.strategy: Arda gives up and sits on the floor.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair, now empty, creeps over and positions itself under him, then collapses flat, leaving him sitting on a folded chair.
beats.newInformation: The chair is attracted to being sat on but cannot support, so it ends up as a flattened seat.

raw.finalPayoff: The chair, now empty, creeps over and positions itself under him, then collapses flat, leaving him sitting on a folded chair.
raw.suggestedPayoffFamily: object agency / goal partially achieved absurdly
raw.loopPotential: Arda might use a different chair, but the same collapse rule may apply to its twin.
raw.providerRationale: Chair's support function is conditionally removed; visible collapse on sitting is classic but we vary with self-moving chair.

references.sourceText: Arda checks the chair, stands it up, and presses on the seat with one hand.
The chair collapses instantly under the light hand pressure, then springs back.
Even partial weight triggers collapse; no weight means rigid.
Arda tries to sit very slowly, easing weight onto the seat.
The chair collapses progressively, lowering him to the floor in a controlled slide, then snaps shut on his fingers.
Slow approach doesn't prevent collapse; it just prolongs the drop.
Arda puts a stack of books on the chair to hold it steady.
The chair stays upright, but when Arda sits on the books, the chair collapses sideways and books scatter.
Distributed weight still triggers collapse as long as it includes Arda.
Arda stands on the chair instead of sitting.
The chair flings him forward like a catapult, launching him onto the desk.
The chair's collapse mechanism can store and release energy when weight is applied.
Arda gives up and sits on the floor.
The chair, now empty, creeps over and positions itself under him, then collapses flat, leaving him sitting on a folded chair.
The chair is attracted to being sat on but cannot support, so it ends up as a flattened seat.

Arda sits, chair flattens beneath him.
The chair, now empty, creeps over and positions itself under him, then collapses flat, leaving him sitting on a folded chair.
The chair, now empty, creeps over and positions itself under him, then collapses flat, leaving him sitting on a folded chair.
The chair is attracted to being sat on but cannot support, so it ends up as a flattened seat.

raw.impossibleRule: Any throw causes the ball to accelerate away from the thrower, gaining speed with distance, until it orbits back and hits nothing.

raw.goalRuleRelationship: The throwing action intended to send ball to friend instead accelerates it away, preventing catch.

beats.newInformation: The ball's acceleration is independent of throw force.

beats.strategy: Kiko runs to intercept the returning ball.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ball swerves around Kiko, gaining more speed, and orbits the yard in a loop.
beats.newInformation: The ball actively avoids being caught.

beats.visibleConsequence: The ball bounces between their gloves, never being caught, and knocks them both over.
beats.newInformation: The ball treats gloves as new launch pads, increasing chaos.

beats.strategy: Luca tries to trap the ball with a bucket.

beats.newInformation: The ball's speed now breaks sound barrier, making it uncatchable and noisy.

beats.strategy: Both give up and walk away.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ball, losing speed, lands gently in Kiko's open hand, then falls asleep with a snore.
beats.newInformation: The ball only becomes catchable when no one is trying to catch it.

raw.title: Book Jumps to End
raw.normalExpectation: Opening book at page 1 shows beginning.

raw.title: Opposite-Color Paintbrush
raw.normalExpectation: Brush applies paint color loaded on it.
raw.impossibleRule: Whatever color you load, the brush deposits the complementary color; loading blue paints orange, loading red paints green.
raw.visibleTrigger: Mimi strokes blue paint; wall turns orange.
raw.whyThisObject: Brush is a transfer tool for pigment; if it inverts color, painting a chosen color is impossible.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action to apply blue paint produces orange, so the wall never becomes blue.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Mimi stands at a wall with a blue paint bucket and brush mid-stroke; the painted patch is vivid orange.

beats.strategy: Mimi mixes a custom color equal parts blue and orange, hoping inversion cancels.
beats.visibleConsequence: The brush paints a shimmering gray that immediately splits into blue and orange stripes.
beats.newInformation: Complementary inversion doesn't cancel but separates into two colors.

beats.strategy: Mimi tries to paint the wall orange, expecting inversion to give blue.
beats.visibleConsequence: The wall turns blue-green, not pure blue, and the brush swirls automatically.
beats.newInformation: The inversion rule includes a hue shift, so aiming for orange doesn't yield blue.

beats.strategy: Mimi uses a roller instead of brush.
beats.visibleConsequence: The roller paints the opposite color at triple scale, covering the wall in a giant orange sunburst.
beats.newInformation: The inversion applies to any painting tool, increasing area.

beats.strategy: Mimi puts a stencil on the wall to paint a pattern.
beats.visibleConsequence: The stencil areas stay original color, while the exposed wall turns complementary, creating a negative of the pattern.
beats.newInformation: The brush inverts color in the open areas, not just strokes.

beats.strategy: Mimi gives up and paints the wall back white.
beats.visibleConsequence: The white paint turns black, then the entire wall flashes and becomes a mirror reflecting the room in inverted colors.
beats.newInformation: Painting white triggers a full-wall color inversion, turning the wall into a funhouse mirror.

raw.finalPayoff: The white paint turns black, then the entire wall flashes and becomes a mirror reflecting the room in inverted colors.
raw.loopPotential: Any new paint attempt may cause new color chaos; the wall can never be one color.
raw.providerRationale: Paintbrush's pigment transfer is inverted; visually clear when blue becomes orange.

raw.title: Opposite Autocorrect
raw.normalExpectation: Typing words sends intended message.
raw.impossibleRule: The phone autocorrects every word to its opposite meaning (e.g., 'yes' becomes 'no', '5' becomes 'five thousand'), and sends instantly before you can edit.
raw.visibleTrigger: Luca types 'Meet at 5' and message sends as 'Melt at five thousand'.
raw.whyThisObject: Phone's autocorrect is supposed to help, but if it inverts meaning, communication is reversed.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action of texting the plan sends the opposite plan, so friend goes to wrong place/time.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Luca looks at phone screen; the sent message reads 'Melt at five thousand' while the intended message is visible above as typed but crossed out.

beats.strategy: Luca types double negatives to get positive meaning.
beats.visibleConsequence: The phone autocorrects to opposite of double negative, resulting in confusing triple negative and message sends 'I won't not never meet'.
beats.newInformation: Inversion is literal but compounds with grammar.

beats.strategy: Luca uses emojis instead of words.
beats.visibleConsequence: Emojis flip to their opposites: thumbs up becomes thumbs down, smiley becomes angry.
beats.newInformation: The autocorrect applies to all symbols, not just text.

beats.strategy: Luca calls instead of texting.
beats.visibleConsequence: His voice comes out reversed, saying 'Meet at five' as 'Evif ta teem', and the friend hears gibberish.
beats.newInformation: The phone's inversion extends to audio, reversing speech.

beats.strategy: Luca uses a different phone, borrowing Mimi's.
beats.visibleConsequence: Mimi's phone also autocorrects, sending 'Don't meet' but then the original phone sends the correct text spontaneously.
beats.newInformation: The rule follows Luca, not the device; only the first phone can sometimes correct itself.

beats.strategy: Luca tries to edit the sent message by appending 'ignore previous', but that also inverts.
beats.visibleConsequence: The friend receives a series of contradictory messages and finally shows up at 5 AM, throwing a pillow at Luca.
beats.newInformation: The accumulation of opposite texts leads to the friend arriving at opposite time.

raw.finalPayoff: The friend receives a series of contradictory messages and finally shows up at 5 AM, throwing a pillow at Luca.
raw.loopPotential: Any future text will be reversed, forcing Luca to speak in person or use smoke signals.
raw.providerRationale: Phone autocorrect is meant to fix errors; reversing meaning creates direct goal interference.

raw.title: Dirtying Washing Machine
raw.normalExpectation: Clothes come out cleaner.
raw.impossibleRule: The machine extracts dirt from clothes and redeposits it onto another item in the same load, so the load comes out with one clean item and the rest soot-black.
raw.visibleTrigger: Arda opens washer, one white shirt pristine, other clothes blackened.
raw.whyThisObject: Washer is meant to remove dirt; if it just moves dirt between items, cleaning is incomplete.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action to wash clothes leaves most dirtier, preventing clean laundry.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Arda looks into open washing machine; a single clean white shirt sits atop a pile of blackened garments.

beats.strategy: Arda separates whites and colors, running two loads.
beats.visibleConsequence: In the white load, dirt migrates to the machine's drum, which turns black and rubs off on all whites.
beats.newInformation: The machine can hold and transfer dirt to its own walls.

beats.strategy: Arda puts all clothes in with extra detergent.
beats.visibleConsequence: The detergent bubbles turn gray, and the clothes come out tie-dyed with dirt patterns.
beats.newInformation: More detergent spreads dirt more evenly, creating stains.

beats.strategy: Arda wipes the drum clean before running again.
beats.visibleConsequence: The wiped drum stays clean, but the clothes now emerge with mud splatters exactly where fabric touched the drum.
beats.newInformation: The machine deposits dirt at contact points, so any cycle dirties.

beats.strategy: Arda uses a mesh laundry bag to isolate each item.
beats.visibleConsequence: Each bag becomes a dirt packet; one bag bursts, sprinkling dry dirt like a pepper shaker.
beats.newInformation: Isolating clothes turns each into a dirt bomb.

beats.strategy: Arda gives up and takes clothes to a river to wash by hand.
beats.visibleConsequence: The washing machine follows him on its spin cycle, rolling down the street, and the clothes he washed in the river absorb dirt from the machine's wake.
beats.newInformation: The machine pursues Arda and re-dirties any clothes he cleans elsewhere.

raw.finalPayoff: The washing machine follows him on its spin cycle, rolling down the street, and the clothes he washed in the river absorb dirt from the machine's wake.
raw.loopPotential: Any washing attempt, anywhere, attracts the machine's dirt.
raw.providerRationale: Washer's cleaning function is reversed into dirt redistribution; visually obvious with one clean item among blackened.

references.sourceText: Arda separates whites and colors, running two loads.
In the white load, dirt migrates to the machine's drum, which turns black and rubs off on all whites.
The machine can hold and transfer dirt to its own walls.
Arda puts all clothes in with extra detergent.
The detergent bubbles turn gray, and the clothes come out tie-dyed with dirt patterns.
More detergent spreads dirt more evenly, creating stains.
Arda wipes the drum clean before running again.
The wiped drum stays clean, but the clothes now emerge with mud splatters exactly where fabric touched the drum.
The machine deposits dirt at contact points, so any cycle dirties.
Arda uses a mesh laundry bag to isolate each item.
Each bag becomes a dirt packet; one bag bursts, sprinkling dry dirt like a pepper shaker.
Isolating clothes turns each into a dirt bomb.
Arda gives up and takes clothes to a river to wash by hand.
The washing machine follows him on its spin cycle, rolling down the street, and the clothes he washed in the river absorb dirt from the machine's wake.
The machine pursues Arda and re-dirties any clothes he cleans elsewhere.
Clean clothes

The washing machine follows him on its spin cycle, rolling down the street, and the clothes he washed in the river absorb dirt from the machine's wake.

beats.strategy: Noah tries to break off a spike by hand.

beats.newInformation: The ice regrows when broken, faster each time.

beats.strategy: Noah runs warm water over the tray to melt spikes.

beats.newInformation: Melted water refreezes into spikes anywhere, not just tray.

raw.normalExpectation: Flashlight produces light beam to illuminate.
raw.impossibleRule: The flashlight absorbs light and projects a darkness beam; pointing it at objects makes them disappear into shadow, while surroundings stay dim.
raw.visibleTrigger: Opa turns on flashlight, a black cone shoots out, making the area darker.
raw.whyThisObject: Flashlight's purpose is to emit light; emitting darkness is its inverse.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action to illuminate keys instead casts them into deeper shadow, preventing search.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Opa points a flashlight at the floor, but a black beam covers the area where keys should be, while the rest of the room is faint.

beats.strategy: Opa shakes the flashlight and changes batteries.
beats.visibleConsequence: The darkness beam becomes wider, swallowing a chair and half the room into blackness.
beats.newInformation: More power increases darkness, not light.

beats.strategy: Opa points the flashlight at the ceiling, hoping reflected light reveals keys.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ceiling turns black and starts dripping shadow like ink, covering the floor.
beats.newInformation: The darkness is a substance that can drip and spread.

beats.strategy: Opa turns on a lamp instead.
beats.visibleConsequence: The lamp works normally, but the flashlight's shadow beam seeks out the lamp and extinguishes it.
beats.newInformation: The darkness beam actively cancels any other light source.

beats.strategy: Opa uses the flashlight in reverse, pointing it at his own eyes.
beats.visibleConsequence: Instead of darkness, a bright beam shines out the back of the flashlight, illuminating a corner where keys are visible.
beats.newInformation: The flashlight has reversed polarity: front emits dark, back emits light.

beats.strategy: Opa picks up the keys using the light from the back.
beats.visibleConsequence: The keys glow and float into the flashlight's front beam, where they vanish into shadow, never to be found.
beats.newInformation: The flashlight's front beam can erase objects, not just darken them.

raw.finalPayoff: The keys glow and float into the flashlight's front beam, where they vanish into shadow, never to be found.
raw.loopPotential: The keys might reappear if Opa uses the back beam, but then the front beam may erase them again.

normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: The flashlight absorbs light and projects a darkness beam; pointing it at objects makes them disappear into shadow, while surroundings stay dim.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Opa points a flashlight at the floor, but a black beam covers the area where keys should be, while the rest of the room is faint. Opa Opa shakes the flashlight and changes batteries.. The darkness beam becomes wider, swallowing a chair and half the room into blackness. More power increases darkness, not light.

escalationPlan.description: Opa points a flashlight at the floor, but a black beam covers the area where keys should be, while the rest of the room is faint. Opa Opa shakes the flashlight and changes batteries.. The darkness beam becomes wider, swallowing a chair and half the room into blackness. More power increases darkness, not light.

Opa Opa points the flashlight at the ceiling, hoping reflected light reveals keys.. The ceiling turns black and starts dripping shadow like ink, covering the floor. The darkness is a substance that can drip and spread.
Opa Opa turns on a lamp instead.. The lamp works normally, but the flashlight's shadow beam seeks out the lamp and extinguishes it. The darkness beam actively cancels any other light source.

Opa Opa uses the flashlight in reverse, pointing it at his own eyes.. Instead of darkness, a bright beam shines out the back of the flashlight, illuminating a corner where keys are visible. The flashlight has reversed polarity: front emits dark, back emits light.

Opa Opa picks up the keys using the light from the back.. The keys glow and float into the flashlight's front beam, where they vanish into shadow, never to be found. The flashlight's front beam can erase objects, not just darken them.

normalizedConcept.finalPayoff: Opa Opa picks up the keys using the light from the back.. The keys glow and float into the flashlight's front beam, where they vanish into shadow, never to be found. The flashlight's front beam can erase objects, not just darken them.

raw.title: Delayed Mirror
raw.normalExpectation: Mirror shows real-time reflection.
raw.impossibleRule: The mirror shows a reflection delayed by one second, so Kiko sees her previous movement; when she moves to adjust, the lag causes her to misreach and bump herself.
raw.visibleTrigger: Kiko raises hand, mirror's hand raises a second later.
raw.whyThisObject: Mirror's function is immediate visual feedback; delay makes self-grooming impossible.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: The action to style hair is based on outdated visual, so hands miss, preventing fixing.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Kiko stands before mirror, her hand raised, but the reflection's hand is still lowered; a ghostly lag overlay is visible.

beats.strategy: Kiko moves slowly, watching the mirror to adjust to delay.
beats.visibleConsequence: The mirror's delay increases to three seconds, and her reflection starts combing hair that Kiko hasn't touched yet.
beats.newInformation: The lag can grow when she tries to compensate.

beats.strategy: Kiko touches her hair while looking down, ignoring the mirror.
beats.visibleConsequence: The mirror shows her reflection looking up and smiling, then her own head tilts involuntarily to match.
beats.newInformation: The delayed reflection can control her current actions, not just display.

beats.strategy: Kiko covers the mirror with a towel.
beats.visibleConsequence: The covered mirror continues to reflect, showing a delayed image on the towel's surface like a screen.
beats.newInformation: The reflection can project onto coverings.

beats.strategy: Kiko turns the mirror around to face the wall.
beats.visibleConsequence: The back of the mirror shows a live feed of Kiko from a second ago on the wall, and she sees herself walking backward.
beats.newInformation: The mirror's delay effect transfers to the wall surface.

beats.strategy: Kiko stands perfectly still until the reflection catches up.
beats.visibleConsequence: The reflection catches up and then freezes, while Kiko's own image splits into two identical Kikos in the room.
beats.newInformation: Synchronizing the delay creates a duplicate Kiko, solving the grooming by having the duplicate fix her hair.

raw.finalPayoff: The reflection catches up and then freezes, while Kiko's own image splits into two identical Kikos in the room.
raw.loopPotential: The duplicate Kiko may also have a delayed reflection, causing infinite twins.
raw.providerRationale: Mirror's real-time reflection is subverted by lag; visually clear when movements don't match.
